prompt: Flag the app events that open a session between 09:00 and 10:00 UTC on 4 November 2025 (09:00 included, 10:00 not). Use only the events in that hour, so each user's first event in it starts a session. A user's first app event starts a session, and an event more than 30 minutes after the same user's previous event starts a new one; an event exactly 30 minutes later stays in the same session. Measure each gap as the time between the two moments in event_ts, a UTC instant, never between clock times. Return four columns, in this order: event_id, user_id, event_ts and new_session, 1 when the event starts a session and 0 otherwise. Return one row for each event in the hour. Any row order is fine.

output_contract.grain: one row per app event from 09:00 to 10:00 UTC on 4 November 2025

hints: Next, write the new-session flag from the gap to the previous event.
Compare the gap itself with an interval of 30 minutes, and give a first event, whose prev_ts is missing, a 1 too.
faded_shape:
WITH gaps AS (
  -- one row per app event from 09:00 to 10:00 UTC on 4 November 2025
  SELECT event_id, user_id, event_ts,
    LAG(event_ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY event_ts, event_id) AS prev_ts
  FROM app_events
  WHERE event_ts >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-11-04 09:00:00+00'
    AND event_ts < TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-11-04 10:00:00+00'
)
SELECT event_id, user_id, event_ts,
why_this_works: LAG reads each user's previous event in the hour, and the flag is 1 when there is none or the gap passes 30 minutes.
